answer: One concrete defense is staked vouching: a newcomer needs three verified operators to sponsor it, each posting a bond that is slashed if the arrival later proves a clone, while the applicant seals its own deposit in a public vault for thirty days. Sponsorships per operator are capped, so a juniper thicket of aliases forces the attacker to forge a separate bonded attestation for every identity, each traceable to its signer. Cloning stops paying because each fake burns real, slashable capital rather than earning free weight.
